bullets.title: Equities close lower; geopolitical tensions, rate fears weigh on broad market
bullets.body: US equities ended near session lows with the S&P 500 down ~0.6%, driven by hawkish US/Iran developments following weekend military activity and rising oil prices (WTI +2.74%, Brent near $100). Internet was the worst tech sub-sector (-2.3%) on geopolitical risk; healthcare notably weak (-2.55%) on trial disappointments. Semis (+1.3%) and communications equipment (+1.4%) bucked the trend. NDX led with Mag 7 lagging all three major indices.

bullets.title: Market pricing ~60% probability of September rate hike; rates rise on hawkish Fed
bullets.body: Treasury 2-year yield rose 1.7 bps to 4.396% and 10-year rose 0.8 bps to 4.792%. Morgan Stanley expects rates on hold through end of 2027 citing hawkish Fed Chair Warsh remarks, while the market is now pricing ~60% probability of a September rate hike. Banks declined 1.3–1.5% and cards/payments fell 2.8% on the higher-rate environment.

bullets.title: $39B 10-year Treasury auction tomorrow likely needs more concession to clear
bullets.body: JPMorgan notes 10-year yields appear ~14bp rich to fundamental drivers, suggesting the upcoming $39B reopening auction will require greater concession. August's 10-year auction cleared 0.1bp cheap with end-user demand at 91.4% (down 0.8%-pts from YTD highs); domestic investment manager takedown fell 0.7%-pts to 73.9%. 30-year momentum has deteriorated with a systematic divergence buy signal triggered; a break above 5.14% would confirm trend continuation, while failure could mean reversion toward 5.00%.

bullets.title: August CPI preview: headline downside risk at 0.34% vs 0.38% consensus
bullets.body: PSC forecasts August headline CPI at 0.34% m/m vs. 0.38% consensus; core CPI in line at 0.21%. Goods deflation is accelerating (Adobe DPI shows sharp deceleration across 18 categories, used cars -0.9% m/m), while energy remains a headwind from Iran conflict. Shelter disinflation expected to accelerate in 1H27. Friday's CPI print is seen as critical for the September FOMC decision.

bullets.title: 22V macro regime shift: consumer slowing, AI capex and earnings momentum to lead
bullets.body: 22V argues the benign slowdown thesis looks increasingly unlikely; mild economic restraint may be needed to restore growth toward trend. Consumer spending is the most vulnerable segment, with a tougher backdrop expected for retail, transports, small caps, and rate-sensitive cyclicals. Leadership is seen rotating toward AI buildout names, earnings momentum stocks, and companies with strong cash returns.

bullets.title: AI capex supercycle confirmed across TMT conference circuit: AVGO, ANET, QCOM, AMD all bullish
bullets.body: At Goldman and Citi TMT conferences, hyperscaler AI capex signals were uniformly strong: AVGO reaffirmed $115B/$230B AI revenue targets for FY27/FY28 with supply (not demand) as the binding constraint; AMD reiterated data center +2x growth in 2027 with MI450 GPU ramping Q3 and CPU supply up 80% in H2:26; ANET cited strong back-end GPU cluster and enterprise campus demand with FY27 margin targets intact; QCOM reiterated $5B FY27 and $15B FY29 data center revenue targets. Room attendance packed across AMD and AMAT sessions, signaling elevated investor interest.

bullets.title: QCOM-AMZN multi-gen AI data center deal: $60B revenue opportunity through 2036
bullets.body: Qualcomm announced a multi-generational custom silicon and optical connectivity collaboration with Amazon covering inference and 1.6T interconnects; AMZN issued QCOM a warrant for up to 25M shares at $161.26, vesting on up to $60B in purchases over 10 years (3.75M shares already vested). Revenue expected to begin in December quarter; Amazon to contribute ~$2B to FY27 data center revenue alongside ByteDance. JPM notes this reinforces conviction in QCOM's $15B FY29 data center target.

bullets.title: NVIDIA acquires Hugging Face for $12.9B; AI infrastructure private markets heating up
bullets.body: NVIDIA confirmed acquisition of Hugging Face for $12.9B including a $1B retention package, and separately invested in Ipronics Programmable Photonics. Anthropic signed a $35B cloud deal with Lambda (NVIDIA-backed) and is likely to name Morgan Stanley and Goldman Sachs as IPO lead underwriters. TSMC acknowledged it cannot keep pace with AI demand despite a fivefold capacity expansion; Korea committed $919B to an 18.4GW AI datacenter buildout by 2035.

bullets.title: Optical/fiber infrastructure rallies: GLW +7.6%, VIAV +11%, LITE +11% on Verizon LTA
bullets.body: Corning signed a multi-billion dollar supply agreement with Verizon for 80M+ miles of high-density optical fiber through 2032, covering both broadband and AI data-center interconnect use cases (~16M fiber miles annually). JPMorgan sees this broadening Corning's AI customer base beyond three announced hyperscalers toward a $1B+ annual DCI revenue run-rate before decade-end. VIAV and LITE surged 11%+ in sympathy on optical networking read-through.

bullets.title: INTC PC CPU prices rising another 10%; upgraded to outperform at Northland
bullets.body: Intel was upgraded to outperform at Northland Capital with PC CPU prices expected to increase another 10%, adding to a server CPU shortage tailwind. INTC closed up 9.1% on the session.

bullets.title: BE joins S&P 500 Sept 21; clean energy and nuclear outperform as sector rallies
bullets.body: Bloom Energy surged 9.6% on S&P 500 inclusion announcement (effective Sept 21). NuScale (SMR) +15.3%, ENPH +6.8%, OKLO +5.0% as clean energy/nuclear outperformed the declining broader market. NEE received a $1.9B DoE loan to restart a nuclear facility in Iowa; global nuclear generation hit a record 2,702 TWh in 2025. Data center REITs also outperformed, up 0.54% YTD with +30.45% performance.

bullets.title: UK gilt yields hit highest since 1998; copper at record highs; credit market quietest post-Labor Day in six years
bullets.body: UK 30-year gilt yields hit their highest level since 1998 on a government debt sale. Copper prices reached record highs on supply constraints and US tariff fears. The US IG debt market is experiencing its quietest post-Labor Day issuance rush in six years, suggesting caution in credit markets despite a still-functioning primary.

bullets.title: OPEC production fell 900K bpd in August; Iran tensions keeping oil elevated
bullets.body: OPEC production fell 900K bpd in August to 19.91M bpd amid Saudi export disruptions linked to geopolitical tensions. US-Iran military activity over the weekend is the primary macro risk cited for the equity sell-off; WTI rose 2.74% on the day with Brent near $100.

bullets.title: Accenture + Google Cloud launch joint agentic AI enterprise deployment unit
bullets.body: Accenture and Google Cloud announced a joint business group specifically targeting enterprise agentic AI deployment, reflecting accelerating enterprise demand for production-grade AI implementation at scale.

bullets.title: NAND structurally upgraded: datacenter AI now primary growth engine; bit growth mid-to-high teens
bullets.body: Citi's Sandisk conference takeaways characterize NAND as entering a structurally stronger demand environment: datacenter is now the primary growth engine (hyperscale AI, KV cache, enterprise SSD) with mid-to-high teens annual bit growth from node transitions. Smartphones, PCs, and edge devices expected to reaccelerate in 2027 with AI-driven higher storage content. SNDK has two-thirds of next-gen memory bits under contract by next year.

bullets.title: US consumer resilient but decelerating; retail and internet underperform
bullets.body: Consumer discretionary underperformed with XLY -0.8% and the retail sub-sector -2.2% on the day. Visa reported US payments volume growing high-single digits with cross-border improving to ~14%, but eBay noted US consumers more resilient than international markets. RV retail data is sharply weak (July -22% YoY). The 22V macro view explicitly flags the consumer as the part of the economy that may need to slow.

bullets.title: OpenAI ChatGPT Images 2.5 launch accelerates generative AI competitive pressure on ADBE
bullets.body: OpenAI launched ChatGPT Images 2.5 across all ChatGPT tiers (desktop, mobile, web), cited by analysts as a direct competitive read for Adobe and creative software incumbents.

bullets.title: CRE CLO distress rate spikes to 28% in August, up 9 percentage points MoM
bullets.body: Green Street data shows CRE CLO distress rate hit 28% in August, up 9 percentage points month-over-month, while CRE price growth is cooling (CPPI +0.8% m/m in August vs. +1.0% in July). Data Center REITs remain a notable outlier, up 30.45% YTD.

bullets.title: Cruise demand robust: zero named storms, bookings mid-to-high single digits ahead of guide
bullets.body: UBS channel checks show cruise bookings up mid-to-high single digits since mid-July, ahead of the mid-single-digit goal, with the peak hurricane season passing with zero named storms on record. Q1 Caribbean, summer Europe, and Alaska bookings are strong across most brands; Norwegian is the outlier, paying 200-300bps higher agent commissions and showing only mid-single-digit bookings. VIK ocean pricing up high single digits for 1H27; Disney high single digits; Norwegian flat-to-negative.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley: rates on hold through end of 2027 on hawkish Warsh commentary
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley explicitly expects the Fed to remain on hold through end of 2027, citing hawkish remarks from Fed Chair Warsh. This view stands in contrast to the market pricing ~60% probability of a September rate hike, creating a contested macro setup heading into Friday's CPI print.
